questions.text: HCAHPS (Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems) is BEST described as:

options.a: A clinical quality measure for hospital-acquired infections
options.b: A standardized national survey measuring patients' perspectives of their hospital care
options.c: An accreditation standard used by The Joint Commission
options.d: A reimbursement model used by Medicare for quality bonuses

questions.explanation: HCAHPS is the first national, standardized, publicly reported survey of patients' perspectives of hospital care. Results are publicly reported and tied to hospital reimbursement through CMS's Value-Based Purchasing program.

questions.text: Patient-centered care is BEST characterized by:

options.a: Physicians making all clinical decisions to maximize efficiency
options.b: Standardized care protocols applied uniformly to all patients
options.c: Respecting and responding to individual patient preferences, needs, and values
options.d: Minimizing patient family involvement to reduce distractions

questions.explanation: Patient-centered care, as defined by the Institute of Medicine, involves respecting and responding to patient preferences, needs, and values, ensuring patient values guide all clinical decisions.

questions.text: A hospital notices its HCAHPS 'communication with nurses' domain score has declined. The MOST appropriate initial step is:

options.a: Immediately replace the nursing staff on low-scoring units
options.b: Analyze the survey data by unit, shift, and patient population to identify patterns
options.c: Dismiss the survey results as statistically insignificant
options.d: Add more nursing staff to all units immediately

questions.explanation: Before taking action, leaders should drill down into the data to understand where, when, and with whom communication is breaking down. This targeted analysis informs effective, evidence-based interventions.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a 'moments of truth' in the patient experience?

options.b: Every interaction a patient has with staff, facilities, and processes during their care
options.c: The quarterly board of directors meeting

questions.explanation: A 'moment of truth' is any point of contact between a patient and the organization that shapes their perception of care quality. Each touchpoint — from parking to discharge — influences the overall patient experience.

questions.text: Shared decision-making between patients and clinicians is MOST important for:

options.a: Reducing the length of clinical consultations
options.b: Ensuring patients choose the least expensive treatment option
options.c: Aligning treatment plans with patient values, preferences, and goals
options.d: Satisfying accreditation requirements for patient rights

questions.explanation: Shared decision-making is a collaborative process where clinicians and patients work together to make care decisions that align with the best available evidence and the patient's personal values, preferences, and circumstances.
